plan.contextChunk: This figure is a perspective drawing of a toroid with a rectangular cross-section, cut open so the reader faces the flat end of the ring. The gray body carries fine radial hatching across its curved upper surface, and the central hole opens through the middle. Across the top, four horizontal dimension arrows stack in registration with a dashed vertical center line: the longest reaches the outer wall and is labeled R2, the next reaches the inner wall and is labeled R1, a third labeled r ends partway out, and a short one labeled dr marks a narrow increment just beyond it. At the right edge a vertical bracket labeled h gives the height of the rectangular face. Inside that face, at radius r, a thin vertical strip of width dr is filled solid orange and tagged da by a curved leader. A red arrow labeled i curls onto the left end of the ring, and two blue curved arrows sweep along the lower body in the direction of the circulating field. Setting one narrow shaded strip against the full cross-section signals that the flux is built up by integrating such elements outward from R1 to R2, which is what the self-inductance calculation requires.

interactions.teaches: A radial slice farther from the toroid axis has a smaller magnetic field because B(r) is proportional to 1/r, so equal-width strips do not contribute equal flux

interactions.label: Flux view
interactions.teaches: The total toroid flux is built by summing the unequal slice contributions from the inner radius R1 outward to R2

demo_steps.title: Single differential strip
demo_steps.narration: The orange da strip marks one radial slice of width dr and height h. Its contribution is dPhi = B(r) h dr, with B(r) evaluated at that radius.

demo_steps.title: Near the inner radius
demo_steps.narration: Move the strip close to R1. The magnetic field is larger near the center, so this same-width strip contributes more flux.

demo_steps.title: Near the outer radius
demo_steps.narration: Move the strip outward toward R2. The strip has the same area, but B(r) is smaller, so dPhi decreases.

demo_steps.title: Build the integral
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the accumulated view: the highlighted region shows all slices swept from R1 to the current r. The logarithmic accumulation comes from integrating 1/r over the rectangular cross-section.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a cut-open rectangular toroid centered on a vertical symmetry axis. Let +X run screen-right from the centerline, +Y run upward, and +Z recede into the page. Use R1 = 1.4 world units, R2 = 3.2 world units, height h = 1.0 world unit, and fixed dr = 0.12 world units. The toroid body is an annular rectangular prism swept around the vertical Y-axis over the rear half of the ring, approximately theta = 0 degrees at the right cut face through theta = 180 degrees at the left cut face, leaving the front half open so the central hole and both rectangular end faces are visible. The right rectangular face lies on the viewer-facing cut plane at the right side; it spans X from R1 to R2 and Y from -0.5 to +0.5. The orange da strip sits on this right rectangular face at X = r, spans Y from -0.5 to +0.5, and has radial width dr. In accumulated-integral mode, fill the right rectangular face region from X = R1 to X = r with translucent orange, while keeping the current strip opaque. The top surface of the toroid is at Y = +0.5 and should show dense thin radial hatching lines from inner to outer radius, especially across the visible upper half of the ring. Body color is light gray #bfbfbf with darker side shading #777777 on the inner wall and cut faces; hatch lines are dark gray #666666; orange strip is #f05a1a; blue field arrows are #008bd2; red current arrow is #d83a3a; dimension lines and labels are black #111111; guide lines are black dashed. Place the dashed vertical centerline at X = 0, running from above the top dimension stack down through the toroid. Put four dimension arrows above the toroid, stacked top to bottom: R2 from X=0 to X=R2, R1 from X=0 to X=R1, r from X=0 to X=r, and dr from X=r to X=r+dr. Draw dashed vertical guide lines at X=0, X=R1, X=r, X=r+dr, and X=R2. The h bracket is to the far right of the rectangular face, slightly outside X=R2, vertical from Y=-0.5 to Y=+0.5. Mathematical values: B(r) = mu0*N*I/(2*pi*r); da = h*dr; dPhi = B(r)*h*dr; accumulated Phi(r) = mu0*N*I*h/(2*pi)*ln(r/R1); total Phi = mu0*N*I*h/(2*pi)*ln(R2/R1); flux linkage N*Phi gives L = mu0*N^2*h/(2*pi)*ln(R2/R1). If numeric readouts are shown, use normalized units with mu0*N*I/(2*pi)=1 unless constants are displayed explicitly.
interactionPlan.notes: Model the toroid as custom BufferGeometry or an extruded annular sector with flat rectangular end caps. Use MeshStandardMaterial with smooth gray shading, but keep dimension arrows and hatch marks as screen-facing black line geometry or CSS2D/SVG overlay so labels remain legible. On slider change, update the orange strip position, the r and dr guide lines, the r arrow endpoint, and the formula readouts. In accumulated mode, show a translucent orange rectangular overlay on the right cross-section from R1 to r and optionally a faint matching swept band over the visible top annular surface; do not remove the current opaque strip. Keep the camera mostly fixed to preserve the textbook view, with no required orbit control.
